description: SURFACED by the fz-rh2.16.2 golden audit. append/quicksort/reverse expected.txt were reblessed for reductions_remaining drift (3998->3997, 3934->3906 [reductions BURNED 66->94, +42%], 3992->3990) -- verified single-line, counter-only, no semantic/alloc change (legit rebless). But this is the SECOND consecutive rebless of the same symptom on the same three fixtures: commit 0aa8dc0eb (fz-79h, 2026-06-18) already reblessed the same reductions_remaining/yield counters once. reductions_remaining is decremented by emit_back_edge_yield_check (native_codegen/terminator.rs ~1229-1249) -- one per cooperative back-edge (tail-loop iteration) check emitted by native codegen; it is a codegen-SHAPE artifact, not semantics. The counts keep drifting UPWARD (more back-edge checks = more work) across intervening commits (type-system/ActivationKey refactors, dead-code removal) that should NOT plausibly change back-edge counts. Per 'tiny-fixture slowness is correctness', repeated same-direction drift is a SIGNAL. INVESTIGATE why compiler-internal refactors keep increasing emitted back-edge-check count for these loops (is the lowering emitting redundant yield checks? is a loop being restructured to iterate more?), rather than reblessing a third time. Not masking wrong output today. Related: fz-rh2.16.2, fz-79h (0aa8dc0eb).

comments.text:
ROOT-CAUSED (spike 2026-07-09, wt-myo, REPORT not fix -- worktree clean, mechanism is correct so nothing to revert). reductions_remaining measures compiled call-graph SHAPE, not source semantics: a reduction is charged per executed tail-call classified as an SCC back-edge (terminator.rs:1234-1253 charges; native.rs:3688-3810 sets is_back_edge iff caller+callee share an SCC in a Tarjan pass over the FULLY-SPECIALIZED native call graph). Because it is a function of the compiled specialization graph, it drifts on ANY internal refactor that reshapes specialization -- with byte-identical output AND allocations.

EVIDENCE (source bytes unchanged across jumps): jump #1 caused ENTIRELY by fz-g58 (63f0fe653, Enum/List planner squash) -- quicksort 26->52 reductions despite quicksort.fz using zero Enum/List/protocol calls (hand-written recursion, graph reshaped underneath). rebless #1 (0aa8dc0eb, fz-79h) pure reconciliation. rebless #2 (2479a69fd, fz-rh2.16.2) states output + every alloc counter byte-identical, only reductions drifted (quicksort 66->94, append 2->3, reverse 8->10); ~250 internals commits in range, not yet bisected. append/quicksort/reverse are canaries: closure-free protocol-free recursive fns with rock-stable alloc profiles, so reductions is the only free value -> exposed nerve for SCC/spec-shape churn other fixtures mask.

CLASSIFICATION: genuine correctness/observability signal (more scheduler-visible yield-check work for identical semantics), NOT benign accounting. Architecturally adjacent to over-specialization (fz-y6w) but not proven identical. Treadmill cause = pinning a codegen-shape metric against programs whose contract is output+allocations. Resolution is de-pin/derive, tracked in children below.

title: reductions_remaining creeps upward on append/quicksort/reverse across unrelated compiler refactors (2nd consecutive golden rebless of the same symptom)
